item.title: François Kevorkian
item.description: For most of 1976 the floor of a Chelsea after-hours club called Galaxy 21 carried live drums until dawn: a French jazz drummer planted in the middle of the crowd, playing along with the records.

item.title: Boogie
item.description: In early 1982 the record every New York floor wanted was D-Train’s “You’re the One for Me”: a gospel-sized baritone riding a bassline that came from a synthesizer, a groove set well below disco tempo, on a twelve-inch from a midtown independent label.
